---
title: "Quick Start"
description: |
  Get from raw vendor files to integrated MRM peaks with INTEGRATOR in a handful of steps.
---

This page is the condensed path from raw files to integrated peaks. Each step links to the full
reference if you need detail.

::: {.callout-tip}
A complete **test dataset** ships with the download — a full set of input and raw-data files you
can use as templates for your own analysis. For a fully worked, real-world analysis with concrete
settings, see the [Dataset 3 workflow ↗](https://slinghub.github.io/mrmhub-workflows/Dataset3.html).
:::

## 1. Convert raw files to mzML

INTEGRATOR reads **mzML**. Convert your vendor files (`.raw`, `.wiff`, `.d`, …) with ProteoWizard
MSConvert (Windows only). → [Vendor → mzML (msconvert)](msconvert.qmd)

## 2. Download the app into your project

INTEGRATOR is a standalone executable — nothing to install. Download the macOS/Windows build from
[Releases](https://github.com/SLINGhub/MRMhub/releases), unzip it into your project folder, and
clear the one-time security prompt. Keeping one copy per project keeps the analysis re-runnable.
→ [Download & Project Setup](setup.qmd)

## 3. Prepare the input files

Drop your `.mzML` files into the `mzML/` folder and fill in three files (templates are included):

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `param.txt` | Global parameters (tolerances, peak-width windows, threads) |
| `batch_info.csv` | Sample list, in processing order, with sample/QC types |
| transition list | Transitions and features to integrate |

→ [Input Files reference](input-files.qmd)

## 4. Run the four steps

Launch **MRMhub** and work through the terminal menu:

1. **Data Validation** — check input files for inconsistencies.
2. **Peak Finding & RT-shift estimation** — produces `RT_matrix.csv`.
3. **Peak Integration** — produces `long.csv` and `quant_raw.csv`.
4. **Generate PDF results** *(optional)* — per-transition / per-sample chromatogram PDFs.

→ [Running INTEGRATOR](running.qmd)

## 5. Review the results

Open **MRMhub-viz** to inspect chromatograms, then refine global or per-feature parameters and
re-run as needed. → [MRMhub-viz Visualizer](viz.qmd)

## 6. Continue in QUANT

Hand `long.csv` to the QUANT R package for the post-processing pipeline:

```r
import_data_mrmhub("path/to/long.csv", import_metadata = TRUE)
```

→ [QUANT documentation ↗](https://slinghub.github.io/MRMhub/quant/)
